correctness.rationale: For every integer n≥3, 0<alpha≤1, unit-circumradius regular polygon vertices and center, a finite-seminorm bounded real-linear extension must preserve constants and is determined by one central linear functional with coefficients summing to one. Average its cyclic conjugates to obtain the mean operator at no larger norm. For that operator, center-to-vertex differences are at most mean chord^alpha, attained by the fixed-vertex distance function (one-Lipschitz in the snowflake metric); vertex pairs force norm ≥1. Thus Lambda_n=max(1,F_n). Chord product Π_j 2sin(pi j/n)=n proves F_prime(0)=log(n)/n>0, and F_doubleprime(alpha)>0 proves strict increase. With F(0)=(n−1)/n<1 and F(1)=(2/n)cot(pi/2n)>1, there is exactly one alpha_n in (0,1). Riemann sums of squared log chords converge to ∫log²(2sin pi t)=pi²/12 by Parseval; discrete cubic-log moments uniformly bounded yield Taylor remainder O(alpha³). Consequently n(F(c/sqrt(n))−1)→−1+pi²c²/24 and root bracketing gives sqrt(n) alpha_n→2sqrt6/pi. Boundary n=3,4 formulas, alpha=1 cotangent formula, and metric alpha>0 domain are consistent. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove universal limits.
residual_risks: Proof depends on standard logarithmic endpoint Riemann-sum domination and classical Fourier/Parseval identity, both checked for correct normalization, without machine-formal certification.
Computed values at finite n are approximations, not an effective uniform finite-n error bound.

value.rationale: The object and invariant are motivated by the qualitative distinction between nonlinear individual McShane extensions (always norm-one) and real-linear simultaneous extension across the prescribed central point. Exact sharp norm and contractivity threshold hold for every polygon size and continuous snowflake exponent, with a non-obvious 2sqrt6/pi limit derived from logarithmic chord variance. This gives a meaningful family-level boundary for linear extension feasibility and a natural, independently useful scalar operator invariant, not an arbitrary finite table or merely a general theorem specialization. The group averaging step is elementary but the sharp crossing and asymptotic are substantive.
residual_risks: No extension beyond finite regular vertex sets plus center, real scalar functions and 0<alpha≤1; does not give the full disk linear extension constant.
